No. For 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-23, NASA FIRMS recorded zero active-fire or thermal-anomaly detections intersecting ASSET-F01.

All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, VIIRS NOAA-20, VIIRS NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day of the period, so the absence of detections isn't due to a data gap.

Some caveats:
- This is satellite thermal detection only. Small, brief, or low-intensity fires, or fires hidden by cloud or dense smoke between overpasses, can go undetected.
- The match rule is that a detection footprint must intersect the asset. The asset's area isn't given in the output, so I can't comment on how large it is relative to the detection pixels.
- The data is near real time, and it could be revised later.

In short, there is no satellite evidence of a fire on this asset in the period, but that doesn't prove none occurred.
